subject: history_social
passage: Before the 1950s, cargo was loaded onto ships piece by piece: sacks, barrels, and crates were lifted aboard by crane and stowed by hand, and a vessel could spend more days in port than at sea. Malcolm McLean, a trucking company owner, reasoned that the slow part was not the voyage but the handling. The solution, in his ______ was to pack goods into identical steel boxes that could be lifted straight from a truck onto a ship. In 1956 his first converted tanker carried 58 such boxes from Newark to Houston, and the standardized container it introduced now carries most of the world's manufactured goods.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "In his view" interrupts the sentence "The solution was to pack goods into identical steel boxes." An interrupting phrase is set off by a pair of commas; the first comma is already there after "solution," so a second comma must follow "view."
explanation.A: Incorrect. A semicolon can't separate the subject "The solution" from its verb "was."
explanation.B: Correct. The comma after "view" completes the pair of commas that sets off the interrupting phrase.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The interrupting phrase opens with a comma, so it can't close with a dash; the two marks must match.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The comma after "solution" opens a pair, so a matching comma must close it after "view."
